pages.lesson:
LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 13.3.1 WORD CLASSES: COMPOUND SENTENCES

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.3: Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why do we join sentences?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify compound sentences from texts
2. construct compound sentences using different coordinating conjunctions

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify compound sentences from texts
   In simple words: practise until you can identify compound sentences from texts. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. construct compound sentences using different coordinating conjunctions
   In simple words: practise until you can construct compound sentences using different coordinating conjunctions. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences in the examples.
2. Explain Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences.
4. Show that you can: identify compound sentences from texts

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences important for a Grade 8 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read a text on the need for consumer protection and identify the compound sentences,
2. Construct compound sentences on a variety of issues including consumer protection using different conjunctions,
3. Join different independent clauses using a drag and drop application or a completion table, in groups,
4. Communication: It is enhanced as the learner communicates ideas clearly when using compound sentences.
5. Consumer protection: It is enhanced as the learner reads texts and constructs sentences on the theme.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we join sentences?
2. How do we join sentences?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify compound sentences from texts
2. construct compound sentences using different coordinating conjunctions

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
